correctness.rationale: Wan proves that the full analytic semiuniversal base is exactly the germ of \(V(ab,bc,ca,de,ef,fd)\), not merely a tangent cone. Writing the ring as the tensor product of two three-axis rings gives a length-four minimal resolution by tensoring the explicit Hilbert--Burch resolutions. The source's nine two-dimensional components give dimension \(2\); projective dimension \(4\) over the six-variable regular ring gives depth \(2\), hence Cohen--Macaulay. The final free rank is \(4\) and all final shifts agree, giving type \(4\) and levelness, so the ring is not Gorenstein. The Hilbert series, multiplicity, singular locus, and \(K_{3,3}\) Stanley--Reisner curve follow exactly from the split monomial ideal. An independent finite Hochster enumeration reproduces the full Betti table and Hilbert data.

value.rationale: The initiating paper's main new obstructed example is defined by an unusually explicit complete Kuranishi germ, so the intrinsic local algebra of that germ is a natural invariant rather than an arbitrary slice. Cohen--Macaulayness is not automatic for a reducible nine-branch deformation space, and type \(4\) shows that this compact Calabi--Yau tangent-bundle Kuranishi base is decisively non-Gorenstein despite arising from split critical equations. The minimal resolution, multiplicity, six-axis singular stratification, and \(K_{3,3}\) tangent-cone curve give a compact reusable structural fingerprint for comparing future obstructed bundle-deformation germs.
